visual_notes.note: The old dark numeral is tentatively 4 with a small circle to its right. Rectangular and curved enclosing strokes overlap under heavy cancellation; the enclosure and old label remain uncertain.
The cancelled long heading word has two tall f-like strokes and another upright in its middle; effilement is tentative, with affinement retained. The raised sur replaces the following cancelled de.

The whole abandoned passage is crossed and bounded by cancellation strokes. Raised wording and local older strikes are difficult to segregate; tentative text and state alternatives are retained instead of reconstructing a grammatical sentence.

The initial old math group beyond R, the Sigma-like overwritten group, the possible tilde and the A subscript remain uncertain. The short prose word between A and l'ens is physically masked and is counted as one unreadable word.

The H-like group beneath Gamma is the closing pair of quotation marks of the following main line, as shown independently in B10; it is not transcribed as a Gamma subscript. The compressed abbreviation bip. remains uncertain.

The raised (ouverte) qui is attached by a leader at arête; its cancellation traverses the latter part of the parenthetical and the following qui. The leading parenthesis and first letters lie below the strike's rising path, so the full cancelled scope is inferred from the continuous word.

The final R is heavily retraced, with an angular older upper stroke and a small detached upper-right mark. Plain R₁ leads the whole-formula alternative, with hat/prime possibilities retained; the numerical subscript 1 is clear.
The last word has a b/d-shaped ascender and a detached mark. Before freezing, the contiguous B21 entendu supports the leading bien reading, while the shape-level d'un alternative remains recorded.

The note was read along its own rotated baseline. The word cercles is distinguished from two separate words by the same intact letter pattern in B23. Larger sloping main-text que/connexes strokes are excluded. Cancelled and inserted words remain tentative where their layers cross; the small comp/corps group is a raised addition.

The target is the lower parenthetical NB note; the upper duplicated note is context. The clauses after elles and et are obscured by crossing main-text strokes. Their alternatives are kept without selecting a mathematically smoother sentence. The last intervalles ouverts is clear.
